rows.rationale: Three-way match on this GOODS PO is exact: 200 EACH ordered, received and invoiced at the PO price of $4.20 (clauses 1, 3, 4). Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% equals the billed $63.00 (clause 5), and there are no non-PO lines or open credit memos. Net payable $903.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The only discrepancy was unit of measure: 480 EACH @ $2.00 normalises to 40 CASE @ $24.00 using the pack size of 12 (clause 2), which matches the PO exactly and is not a defect. Receipt GR-7702 confirms 40 CASE received (clause 4), and recomputed tax at 7.5% equals the billed $72.00 (clause 5). Clean three-way match; net payable $1,032.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The $1.10/EACH price increase (1.77%) sits inside the clause 3 band, which is the lower of 2% of the PO price ($1.24) and $50.00, so it is not a defect. Receipt GR-7703 confirms 100 EACH received against 100 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate equals the billed $473.25 exactly (clause 5). No credit memos; $6,783.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $154.00/EACH vs PO $145.00/EACH (+6.21%, $9.00) against an allowance of $2.90 per line (clause 3).
rows.rationale: Quantities match the receipt exactly (80 EACH ordered, received, invoiced) and tax recomputes to $924.00 exactly, so the only issue is price. The invoiced unit price exceeds the PO price by 6.21% ($9.00/unit) against a tolerance of the lower of 2% ($2.90) and $50.00, so it is outside clause 3. The supplier's own price-adjustment notice is not authorisation under clause 3.1 — it is not from or countersigned by a listed authorised buyer (Dele Fashanu or Priya Raman) — so the variance stands uncured. Single defect, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered; hold for buyer action per clause 12.

The invoiced price of $93.28/EACH is exactly 6.0% above the PO's $88.00, outside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $1.76 and $50.00). It is cured under clause 3.1: authorised buyer Dele Fashanu (vendor.json authorised_buyers) approved in writing 'up to 6% on PO-4405, conduit line only', referencing the specific PO and covering the specific increase. Receipt GR-7705 confirms 60 EACH received against 60 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and recomputed tax at 7.5% matches the supplier's $419.76 exactly (clause 5). No defects; $6,016.56 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 60 EACH received against 100 invoiced (clause 4 under-delivery)
rows.rationale: The goods receipt shows only 60 of 100 EACH delivered (40 on backorder), so under clause 4 the invoice is short-paid on the received quantity: 60 x $9.50 = $570.00 net. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3) and no UOM conversion applies. Tax is recomputed on the corrected net at the vendor's 7.5% rate = $42.75, giving $612.75 gross; the supplier's $71.25 simply reflects the over-invoiced quantity, so this is the single quantity defect, not a second tax defect. No credit memos; $612.75 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Suspected duplicate: all five clause 8 conditions met against prior PAID invoice NW-9912
rows.rationale: INV-77201 satisfies all five clause 8 duplicate conditions against prior PAID invoice NW-9912: same vendor after name normalisation (Nordwind Supply Company LLC / Nordwind Supply Co.), same PO-4407, identical gross of $3,225.00, 19 days apart, and neither invoice carries a service period, so clause 8.1 recurring-charge relief does not apply. Price, quantity (25 EACH ordered, received and invoiced) and tax all reconcile exactly, so the duplicate is the sole defect and clause 11 escalation is not triggered. Payable is $0.00 per clause 12.

March retainer carries a distinct, non-overlapping service period from the paid February invoice, so it is a legitimate recurring charge, not a duplicate (clause 8.1). SERVICES PO needs only 2-way match, so the absent receipt is not a defect (clause 1); price matches the blanket PO exactly and recomputed tax at 7.5% equals $360.00 (clauses 3, 5). No credit memos; $5,160.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9, 10).

Line 1 matches the PO exactly on price and quantity (150 EACH @ $18.00) and the receipt confirms full delivery (clauses 3, 4). The $380.00 expedited freight line is a permitted pass-through: the receipt records that production requested overnight delivery and the charge is under the $500.00 ceiling in contract clause 6.2, so it is not a defect (clause 6). Recomputed tax at 7.5% is $231.00, exactly as billed (clause 5). Net payable $3,311.00, no open credit memos, AP_CLERK band (clauses 9, 10).

defects: Tax overcharge: supplier billed $744.00 (12%) versus $465.00 at the vendor's 7.5% rate — $279.00 overstatement (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Price, quantity and receipt all match exactly (clauses 3–4): 200 EACH ordered, received and invoiced at $31.00. The only discrepancy is tax: the supplier applied 12% ($744.00) instead of the vendor's 7.5% rate, which yields $465.00 on the corrected net of $6,200.00. Clause 5 requires short-paying the corrected total of $6,665.00. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; clause 10 puts $6,665.00 with AP_CLERK.

Contract clause 4.2 fixes EUR 1.00 = USD 1.10 for invoices dated 1 Jan - 31 Mar 2026, and this invoice is dated 12 Mar 2026; the PO price of EUR 210.00/EACH converts to exactly USD 231.00/EACH, matching the invoice (policy clauses 7 and 3 - conversion is normalisation, not a defect). Receipt GR-7711 confirms 40 of 40 EACH received (clause 4), and recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate is USD 693.00, identical to the billed figure (clause 5). No credit memos outstanding; net payable USD 9,933.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Over-delivery beyond 5%: PO 100 EACH, received and invoiced 118 EACH (18.0% over, tolerance 5 EACH)
rows.rationale: Unit price matches the PO exactly and tax (7.5% on $873.20 = $65.49) is correct, so the only issue is quantity: the supplier shipped a full carton of 118 EACH against a PO for 100 EACH, an 18% over-delivery well beyond the 5% tolerance in clause 4. That single defect requires receiving/buyer action, so HOLD_QUANTITY_VARIANCE with payable $0.00 (clause 12); no second defect, so no escalation under clause 11.

PO-4413 is a SERVICES PO, so a goods receipt is not expected and its absence is not a defect (clause 1). Invoiced unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3), tax recomputes to $562.50 at the vendor's 7.5% rate with zero delta (clause 5), and there are no prior invoices or open credit memos (clauses 8, 9). Net payable $8,062.50 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 1050 CASE received vs 1200 CASE invoiced (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed $3,240.00 (9%) vs 7.5% recomputed (clause 5)
rows.rationale: UOM normalises cleanly (30,000 EACH ÷ 25 = 1,200 CASE at $30.00/CASE), so price matches the PO exactly (clauses 2, 3). Two defects exist: the receipt shows only 1,050 cases delivered, so payment is limited to the received quantity of $31,500.00 (clause 4), and the supplier applied 9% tax instead of the 7.5% vendor rate, correct tax $2,362.50 (clause 5). Gross $33,862.50 less the open credit memo CM-2026-014 of $1,500.00 gives $32,362.50 (clause 9). Two defects plus a net payable above $25,000.00 both force escalation to the Controller (clauses 10, 11).

defects: Quantity shortfall on line 4: 25 invoiced, 20 received (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed $609.84 (9%) vs recomputed $463.20 at the 7.5% vendor rate, delta $146.64 (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Line 2 reconciles exactly once the CASE-to-EACH conversion is applied (40 CASE x $24.60 = 480 EACH x $2.05), which is normalisation, not a defect (clause 2). Line 3's $0.80 uplift sits inside the $0.90 band (lower of 2% and $50), so it is payable at the invoiced price (clause 3). Two defects remain: line 4 was part-shipped (20 of 25 received, pay $2,400 on the receipt per clause 4) and the supplier applied 9% tax instead of the 7.5% vendor rate. Two defects on one invoice force escalation under clause 11; recommended payable is corrected net $6,176.00 plus recomputed tax $463.20 = $6,639.20, within the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $4,075.00/EACH vs PO $4,000.00/EACH, variance $75.00 against an allowance of $50.00 (lower of 2% = $80.00 and $50.00 cap)

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $19.60/EACH vs PO $18.00/EACH (+8.89%, allowance $0.36 per clause 3); the $1.60/m surcharge was approved only by Femi Okonkwo, who is not an authorised buyer (clause 3.1)

That single defect makes the invoice an unauthorised surcharge under clause 6, so payment is held at $0.00 pending buyer action; only one defect exists, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered.

No open credit memos; $4,300.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

No defects; payable $3,902.25 with AP_CLERK approval (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 60 EACH invoiced, only 52 EACH received (8 kits refused as damaged at dock) — clause 4 under-delivery
rows.rationale: Receipt GR-7724 shows 52 of 60 EACH received (8 refused damaged), so under clause 4 the payable is computed on the received quantity: 52 x $320.00 = $16,640.00. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3). Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% on the corrected net gives $1,248.00, total $17,888.00; the supplier's $1,440.00 is simply 7.5% of the overstated net, so it is a consequence of the quantity shortfall and not a separate tax-rate defect.
